subject: Post-demo: concurrency qualification & rateband ask (Mendocroft)
body:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Ben Hargrove <ben.hargrove@mendocroft.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@corp-mendocroft.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: concurrency qualification & rateband ask (Mendocroft)

Thanks again for the demo slot earlier — appreciate the run-through, Ben and Priya. This note captures the performance targets and the specific concurrency / connection requirements we discussed and a short ask so we can size a pilot rateband.

Quick summary of what we heard on the call:
- Latency SLO: 99th pct < 200ms for single-turn responses up to ~512 tokens (longer generative chains okay but classified separately).
- Throughput profile: baseline sustained QPS ~80, expected burst behavior up to ~250 QPS for 60–90s windows during peak events.
- Concurrency: each user opens 1 websocket for streaming result; some power users will have 2 concurrent streams. Expect ~30–50 concurrent active websocket connections in pilot, up to ~100 in prod.
- Streaming: partial-delivery (server-sent / websocket) with per-token latency constraints; keepalive / idle timeout ~5m.

Open questions we raised on the call that will affect rateband sizing:
1) Are bursts per-account or per-API-key? (affects whether we size at account or key-level).
2) Will users multiplex multiple active prompts on a single socket, or open separate sockets per prompt?
3) Does Mendocroft require regional affinity (us-west) for lower tail latency?

Ask from Redwood: if the high-level numbers below look right, please confirm so we can issue a pilot rateband + credit estimate and a proposed fallback policy. Attached: redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf (rate tiers) and conn-profile.csv (example connection assumptions).

Proposed pilot band (initial):
- Sustained QPS: 100
- Burst cap (60s sliding): 220 QPS
- Concurrent streaming connections: 40
- API-level rate limits: per-API-key primary; optional per-account aggregate

Next steps: please confirm the burst model and whether the 2x-power-user streams are expected. If confirmed, we will send a short MOP (mutual action plan) and a draft rateband that includes soft-429 behavior and fallback model details.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 15:34:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: concurrency qualification & rateband ask (Mendocroft)

Thanks Aditya — this is a great start. A few clarifications from our side:
- Bursts should be considered per-account (we operate with several API keys under one account for internal teams). We can surface per-key QPS but accounting is at account level.
- Typical sustained traffic in sandbox -> prod ramp: start ~20 QPS during pilot ramp, expect sustained ~80 QPS in steady pilot usage, but we have event-driven spikes (marketing pushes) that can hit ~250 QPS for short windows.
- Streaming model: users will generally open one socket; power users may open two concurrent sockets during advanced flows. We don't multiplex multiple prompts over a single socket.

Two asks: can Redwood confirm whether prefix/KV caching helps reduce token cost for our use-case (we have common system prompts), and whether connection multiplexing (multiple logical streams over a single TCP) is supported or recommended?

I'll loop Priya on procurement timing — we want to get pilot live in June if possible.

-ben
Ben Hargrove
Head of Platform Engineering, Mendocroft

Ben — good notes. A couple operational clarifications from infra/limits perspective:
- Redwood exposes both: connection_limit (max concurrent websocket connections per API key) and concurrent_streams (active generation sessions). We can map these onto "per-key" limits and optionally enforce an account-level aggregate.
- Prefix / KV caching: yes — for repeated system prompts and shared prefixes we can enable prefix caching which reduces compute per-token and effectively increases sustainable QPS for the same hardware footprint. We'll include expected token savings in the rateband doc.
- Multiplexing: we support HTTP/2 multiplexing on our private deployments and certain edge proxies; for hosted websockets typical deployment is 1 socket per logical stream — multiplexing adds complexity for tail latency on partial deliveries, so we usually don't recommend it for streaming-first UX.

I'll draft a succinct rateband option set (pilot / prod) and pass to Grace to finalize the crediting/overage approach.

- Soojin

Couple more items before we sign off on pilot sizing:
- Fallback behavior: if Redwood needs to shed load, do you automatically fail requests with 429, or can you gracefully fall back to a smaller model variant for continued partial service? What's the expected tail behavior and whether fallbacks are within the rateband or incur extra cost?
- Regional affinity: can you guarantee deploying instances with us-west edge routing for the pilot to minimize tail latency?

If we can get written confirmation on those two, we'll be comfortable moving to the MOP and a PO.

-ben

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: concurrency qualification & rateband ask (Mendocroft)

Hi Ben / Priya — thanks for the fast turn. Below is a proposed rateband and fallback policy (high level) we can include in the pilot MOP. Attaching the full ratecard for numbers.

Proposed ratebands (pilot):
- Sustained QPS: 100 (per-account)
- Burst cap (60s sliding window): 220 QPS
- Concurrent streaming connections: 40 (per-account), per-key soft limit default 30
- Idle socket timeout: 5m (configurable)

Prod suggestion (subject to sizing + commitment):
- Sustained QPS: 200
- Burst cap (60s): 600
- Concurrent streaming connections: 100

Fallback and throttling behavior:
- Soft throttling: incremental 429s above per-key limit with backoff headers (Retry-After) — during soft-throttle window we can optionally route to a lower-cost model variant (e.g., redwood-small) for partial responses; fallback behavior is opt-in and billed at the fallback model rate.
- Hard limit: sustained over-limit beyond agreed grace will trigger request rejection (429) until usage returns to band.
- Credit & overage: for pilot we can extend a small trial credit (applied after first invoice) to cover measured overage while we tune limits.

Operational asks for Mendocroft:
- Confirm per-account billing and whether you want per-key hard limits.
- Confirm expected peak concurrency per region (us-west preferred).

If Mendocroft confirms the per-account burst model and us-west affinity, we'll publish a 1-page MOP and a short SCOPED rateband table for signature.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com

Thanks Grace — that all looks good. Confirming:
- Per-account burst accounting is fine (we will manage API keys per-team).
- Please enable us-west affinity for pilot.
- We opt-in to the fallback-to-smaller-model feature during soft-throttle windows (please include expected latency/cost tradeoffs in the MOP).

Next steps:
1) Redwood to share the 1-page MOP + scoped rateband (and the updated ratecard you attached).
2) Mendocroft to issue PO for pilot (Priya to confirm timeline) and sign a short SOW for pilot scope.
3) Schedule onboarding call (technical) — suggested window next Wed 10–12 PT.

If you can send the MOP today we'll kick procurement.

Best,
